about: Ultimatum is the rarest Cabernet in the Goldschmidt family’s range. Nick Goldschmidt, a New Zealander with degrees in viticulture and enology, came to Sonoma in 1989, became chief winemaker at Simi and later led winemaking for Allied Domecq and Beam Estates. With his wife Yolyn he built a label of single-vineyard wines from Alexander Valley and Napa Valley’s Oakville appellation, where the family’s Game Ranch Cabernet has drawn high scores for two decades.

Double Rock is a two-acre block on a steep knoll above Game Ranch, midway between Highway 29 and the Silverado Trail and facing north-northwest. Planted in 1988, it is farmed by hand and organically; the stones gathered from the rows are piled beneath the vines, which gives the vineyard its name. The old vines bear loose clusters of tiny berries with a high ratio of skin to juice. The 2018 is 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, a selection of just two barrels, held back for extra bottle age before release.

The Wine Advocate found pencil shavings, black cherry and raspberry, silky tannins, mouthwatering acidity and a long, dusty finish, and gave it some 20 more years. James Suckling noted a mint-chocolate edge to blackberry and cedar alongside dark plum and forest floor. At eight years old it is only beginning to open.
